$comment: The collector output contract of issue #926 (parent #817): one result file per issued work item and one match file per waiting key, both written once by the collector and validated independently by submit-results.mjs before anything is posted. Lengths, vocabularies and bounds are the API's own (Inventory.Domain.PriceCatalogue and InventoryApi.DTOs, issues #937 and #941), restated here so a file that could never be accepted is refused before a request is made. Two rules cannot be expressed in this document and live in output-schema.mjs beside it: which fields require which other fields, and that a search the page cap stopped is reported as truncated.

runId.description: The run the work list issued.

workItemId.description: The issued work item this file answers.

outcome.description: What happened to the search. not_searched is the run completion's answer and never a collector's.

failureReason.description: Why it failed, for a failed search and for no other.

paging.description: What the search read, so a page cap cannot be reported as a complete search.

rows.description: One row per supplier product id this search kept as a real match, any pack size.

workItemId.description: Optional, and must be the file's own.

barcode.description: Text, so a leading zero survives.

packQuantity.description: Left out when unknown, never sent as 0.

supplierGstRate.description: A proportion, when the supplier publishes one.

stockStatus.description: Optional: a missing or unrecognised value is submitted as unknown, never a reason to drop a row.

observedAtUtc.description: Do not write it: the submitter sets it to when this file was written, replacing any value given.

sourceUrl.description: The supplier's own page the row was read from.

matchFile.$comment: price-collector-out/match-<waiting-key>.json. The authoritative key is the waitingKey inside the file, never the file name.

waitingKey.description: Exactly as the work list published it.

masterProductId.description: One existing master product, or a suggested new one - never both.

confidence.description: high only when brand, variant and size clearly agree and only one master product fits.

reason.description: The short evidence a reviewer reads.
